doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: You'll Never Forget Me, her grandmother's death at the Vanguard, and later days with Miles
summary: The song was first planned with Miles at the Vanguard until her grandmother died; later they shared dressing rooms in Paris and Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: What about the Kettle [phonetic] collection? You were to have recorded that some years earlier.

That‘s right. I did that in the Vanguard, and I found out my grandmother had died. My grandmother was so special to me, and I couldn‘t sing the song. In fact, I couldn‘t finish out the week. I said, ―John, I just can‘t do it.‖ I couldn‘t sing. I couldn‘t do anything. So he got Tommy Flanagan to finish out the week, and I was saying goodbye to Miles. I said, ―I‘ve got to go. Grandma‘s gone. But that song,‖ I said, ―we‘re going to record that one day together.‖ And he says, ―A beautiful song.‖ You’ll Never Forget Me, that was it, and that‘s back in 19, I guess about ‘63 or something like that. Good lord, I‘m just telling my age. Wow, ‘63. But we had wonderful times together toward the end, because we were in Paris together. We did that outdoor theater that was magnificent, more than ten thousand people. It looked like they were standing straight up. The seats were just up like that. We were there together. We were at the beautiful theater in Philadelphia. We had dressing rooms right across from each other, and we used to . . . ―How you think my hair looks? What should I put on?‖ I said, ―Those colors are kind of clashing to you.‖ ―You don‘t like this costume? Hell, no.‖ Oh, boy.
